title: Consumption Split Packaging Matrix
author: Aria Chen
body:
Summary:
This document defines the Consumption Split Packaging Matrix: a repeatable framework for mapping multi-dimensional consumption (tokens, embeddings, sessions) across service tiers, fidelity variants, and deployment footprints into compact commercial packages. The goal is to provide sales and product teams with a deterministic, auditable way to convert observed consumption patterns into package recommendations, migration guidance, and billing signals that align with SLOs and unit economics.

Audience:
- Product managers who design offering bundles
- Pricing & finance for revenue modeling and crediting rules
- Solutions and sales engineers for customer proposals
- Engineering (runtime & billing) for telemetry requirements and enforcement

Goals:
- Create a single canonical matrix that maps consumption vectors to package SKUs and recommended entitlements.
- Ensure consumer-facing packages preserve key SLOs (p50 latency <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms for transactional tiers; batch/embedding tiers have 95% within 5s).
- Minimize surprising bill shocks via clear fallback and overage rules.
- Enable predictable migration paths from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private with consistent economics.

Scope:
- Covers hosted and dedicated capacity tiers; private deployments addressed only for commercial mapping (not infra ops).
- Applies to generation (tokens), conversational sessions, and embeddings. Does not change per-model variant pricing; those are handled by variant SKUs.

Key definitions:
- Consumption Vector: [tokens_generated_per_minute, average_session_length, embedding_requests_per_minute, peak_concurrency].
- Fidelity Variant: qualitative label for a model variant (high, standard, compact) that affects token cost multipliers and latency profiles.
- Package SKU: commercially sold bundle with committed throughput, SLO commitments, and soft caps.

Packaging Matrix (illustrative):
| Tier | Typical use case | Metric shape (example) | Committed throughput | Included credits | Notes |
|------|------------------|------------------------|----------------------|------------------|-------|
| Starter | MVP, low volume dev | tokens 0-5k/min, concurrency <= 2 | 5k tokens/min | 100k tokens/month + 1k embeddings | overage billed at headline rate + 20% |
| Scale | Web app features, sensible defaults | tokens 5k-50k/min, concurrency <= 20 | 50k tokens/min | 2M tokens/month + 20k embeddings | supports burst to 2x for 10 minutes |
| Enterprise Transactional | High SLA product flows | tokens 50k-500k/min, concurrency <= 200 | 500k tokens/min | custom credits & dedicated queue | SLA-backed latency, optional warm capacity |

Pricing heuristics and formulas:
- Base token unit (U_token): headline cost for 1k tokens at standard fidelity.
- Fidelity multiplier (M_fid): high=1.6, standard=1.0, compact=0.65.
- Throughput credit conversion: committed_throughput_tokens_per_minute * 60 * 24 * 30 = monthly throughput capacity in tokens.
- Effective monthly credit used by customer = observed_monthly_tokens * M_fid.
- Overages: billed at base rate * 1.25 if monthly utilization > 110% of committed credits.

Example calculation (Scale SKU):
- Committed throughput: 50k tokens/min -> monthly capacity = 50,000 * 60 * 24 * 30 = 2.16B tokens/month.
- Customer observed tokens (standard fidelity) = 1.5B tokens/month -> usage fraction = 69%. No overage.
- If uses high-fidelity variant (M_fid=1.6) effective usage = 2.4B -> triggers negotiation/overage.

Consumption split rules (how to allocate mixed workloads):
1) Classify traffic by route tags: transactional, background-batch, embedding.
2) Map each tag to preferred tier (transactional->Scale/Enterprise, background->Starter/Scale, embedding->Embedding-tier).
3) Apply fidelity multipliers per route and compute per-route effective credits.
4) Reconcile per-tenant totals to package SKUs using the matrix (prefer highest-fitting SKU where >70% of consumption is within SKU envelope).

Migration & packaging playbook (step-by-step):
1. Telemetry audit (Product & Engineering): validate that the last 90 days of telemetry include token counts, p50/p95 latencies per route, session lengths, embedding counts. Required fields: route_id, model_variant, timestamp, tokens, latency_ms, tenant_id.
2. Consumption vector aggregation (Pricing): build the 90-day percentile vector and simulate fidelity shifts (10/25/50% movement to higher fidelity).
3. Map vector to candidate SKUs using the matrix. If multiple SKUs match, prefer the smaller SKU with a migration credit for first 30 days.
4. Customer proposal (Sales): propose SKU + migration buffer (10-20% headroom) + recommended warm capacity if latency SLO flagged.
5. Engineering rollout (Runtime): assign routing policy (preferred tier, failover tier), set quota and throttles, configure telemetry tags for billing reconciliation.
6. Review & sign-off (Product + Finance): verify expected ARR, projected overages, and SLO margin.

Enforcement & runtime integration requirements:
- Billing signals (per-tenant): monthly_tokens, effective_tokens (post-fidelity), embedding_count, peak_concurrency. These must be emitted by runtime and consumed by billing pipeline.
- Quota service integration: support soft caps with warning thresholds at 70%, 90%, 100% and hard caps with configurable grace windows.
- Fallback policy: when committed throughput exhausted, policy options: a) degrade to compact variant, b) queue requests up to 5s, c) fail with 429 (customer-configurable).

Example runtime JSON config (policy snippet):
{
  "sku": "scale-50k",
  "commit_tokens_per_minute": "50000",
  "fidelity_policy": {"preferred": "standard", "fallback": "compact"},
  "overage_policy": {"threshold_percent": "110", "billing_rate_multiplier": "1.25"}
}

Rollout checklist (go-to-market + operations):
- Product: matrix approved by pricing council and legal
- Finance: simulator shows no negative unit economics at 30% overage scenarios
- Engineering: telemetry coverage >99% for required fields
- Sales enablement: template proposal, FAQ for common migration questions
- Support: runbook for customer on-boarding issues and expected escalations

Metrics and dashboards (required):
- SKU utilization heatmap (daily): percent of committed throughput used across tenants
- Effective fidelity drift (weekly): % of requests using higher-than-default fidelity per tenant
- Overage alerts: triggered when projected monthly utilization crosses 95% of commit and rising trend >5%/day
- SLA impact gauge: correlation of fidelity swaps to p95 latency deviation per route

Commercial guardrails and escalation:
- Pilot customers can be given 30 days migration credits capped at $X (finance to set X per deal size).
- Any >25% delta between projected and observed effective usage after 60 days requires pricing council review.

Ownership and next steps:
- Product (owner): Aria Chen — finalize matrix and maintain revisions.
- Pricing & Finance (owner): Liam Patel — implement simulator and P&L scenarios.
- Engineering (owner): Noah Adler — implement telemetry contract, quota enforcement, and fallback hooks.
- Timeline: finalize draft by 2026-09-17, pilot with 3 customers Q4 2026, GA Q1 2027.

Appendix A — Simulation knobs (for pricing team):
- fidelity_shift_percent (array): [0, 10, 25, 50]
- warm_capacity_multiplier: float (1.0-3.0)
- overage_blend_factor: float (0-1)

Appendix B — Frequently asked questions (short):
Q: Does this change per-variant public pricing?
A: No. Variant list prices remain. This matrix determines how consumption maps to packages and when overage negotiations are triggered.

Q: How do we handle mixed-hosting (hosted + private)?
A: Private customers receive a commercial mapping but separate infra billing. The matrix is used only to recommend entitlements and expected credits.

Related artifacts (to be produced):
- Pricing simulator workbook (Finance)
- Sales proposal templates (Go-to-market)
- Telemetry contract PR (Engineering)

Notes for reviewers:
- Evaluate whether fidelity multipliers reflect current model economics (request model-cost inputs from Applied ML).
- Confirm SLO thresholds for new Enterprise Transactional SKU with SRE.
